quote.quote: On August 2nd, 2024, we convened a Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee and posed three questions to the panel.
A Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee (GeMDAC) meeting was held on August 2, 2024.

recommendation.text: The committee voted 11 yes / 5 no that the results of trial NPC-002 in concert with the additional data support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective in the treatment of patients with NPC. The general consensus was that the 5DNPCCSS and R4DNPCCSS scales were adequate to measure improvement, and that the additional clinical data was consistent with the trial, though members expressed concerns about limitations of the nonclinical data.

quote.quote: The majority of the Committee members (yes: 11 / no: 5) agreed that the results of trial NPC-002 in concert with the additional data support a conclusion that arimoclomol is effective in the treatment of patients with NPC.

linkages.concern: Advisory committee members (particularly the 'No' voters) expressed concern that the data did not meet evidentiary standards for effectiveness, with specific concerns about the limitations of the nonclinical data (apparent lack of randomization and blinding, and lack of PK data because the drug was administered in the drinking water) and agreement that those data did not support treatment effectiveness.
linkages.change: FDA did not grant the applicant's proposed broad NPC monotherapy indication; instead the approved indication was restricted to use in combination with miglustat, because of the uncertainty regarding the efficacy of arimoclomol monotherapy.

concern_quote.quote: For the non-clinical data, the Committee members expressed concerns with the apparent lack of randomization and blinding, and the lack of PK data, given that the drug was administered in the drinking water, and agreed the data did not support treatment effectiveness.

change_quote.quote: Given the uncertainty (based on the submitted clinical, nonclinical, and clinical pharmacology data) regarding the efficacy of arimoclomol monotherapy, it will be approved for use in combination with miglustat.

summary: For this Class 2 Resubmission (after a first-cycle Complete Response), FDA convened the Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee on August 2, 2024, posing three questions on the adequacy of the efficacy data for arimoclomol in NPC. The committee found the disease-severity scales adequate but voiced concerns about the nonclinical data, and voted 11 yes / 5 no that the trial plus additional data support effectiveness; that favorable majority supported FDA's decision to approve. The documents bundle the AdComm with other internal reviews (L4112) as inputs to the outcome that arimoclomol be approved only in combination with miglustat, and attribute that restriction to uncertainty about monotherapy efficacy, so the specific concern-to-restriction link is inferred rather than explicitly stated.
